gate_claims.claim: formal.cover takes the proof's own setup file and runs it in cover mode from a copy, so the script, engines, depth and assumptions are the proof's; the copy differs only in mode cover and absolute file names
a cover for the antecedent of each assertion is written into a copy of the design file, and the run fails when one is never reached
an assertion with no implication has no antecedent and is counted as always checked (unguarded)
the antecedent covers are derived for a top-level |-> or |=> or a procedural assertion
the cover check refuses to run, before anything is executed, when an antecedent cannot be derived (the check runs before the tool starts)

the refusal names a sequence operator, a nested implication, a named property inside an expression, a named sequence, an action block, a deferred assertion, and a macro that asserts and cannot be expanded
the refusal is made by _sby_cover_check from the derivation's underived list
a setup with no cover at all fails, and one whose covers are all unreached fails (run locally, setups A and C)
an unreached cover fails the run with vacuous: n of m covers never reached
an unreached antecedent fails the run: the assertion is never checked
a form the derivation cannot handle is refused by the cover run with file, line and reason
the tool takes sby (required) and sources
the cover check runs single-task setups only: a setup with [tasks] is refused
a setup with no [options] section is refused
the cover copy sets only mode cover, so cover_assert is the proof's own option and defaults to off: a cover reached by breaking an assertion passes unless the setup sets cover_assert on (run locally)
the must-fail scorer can require the cover check on the clean files before it tries any mutant, so every cover is reached
the cover check's own parse of the log reports counts of covers and antecedents reached
